y space equals a x squared plus b x plus c

blocks.md:
- Completing the square is another method used to solve quadratic equations
- It simply means writing $y=ax^{2}+bx+c$ in the form $y=a(x+p)^{2}+q$
- It can be used to help find other information about the quadratic like coordinates of the turning point

blocks.text: How do I complete the square?

blocks.md: The method used will depend on the value of the *coefficient* of the **x**<sup>**2**</sup> term in $y=ax^{2}+bx+c$

- p is half of b
- q is c - p<sup>2</sup>

blocks.alt: Completing the square Notes Diagram 1, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md:
- You first need to take $a$ out as a factor of the x<sup>2</sup> and x terms
- Then continue as above

blocks.alt: Completing the square Notes Diagram 2, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.text: When is completing the square useful?

blocks.md:
- Completing the square helps us find the **turning** **point** on a quadratic graph
- It can also help you **create the equation** of a quadratic when given the turning point

blocks.alt: Completing the square Notes Diagram 3, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md: - It can also be used to **prove** and/or **show** results using the fact that a squared term will always be greater than or equal to 0

blocks.alt: Completing the square Notes Diagram 4, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
- Sometimes the question will explicitly ask you to complete the square
- Sometimes it will even remind you of the form to write it in
- But sometimes it will expect you to spot that completing the square is what you need to do to help with other parts of the question... like finding turning points!
